title: Chords A Bm G D 2x 120bpm two strums each
sourceAudio: ../audio/Chords A Bm G D 2x 120bpm two strums each.mp4
timingNotes: Player's description: downstrum on the beat, let it ring, upstrum on the next beat, then mute. So each chord spans 2 beats (1000ms at 120bpm) and contains TWO strums of the SAME chord -- the second attack sits ~500ms into each event, at roughly 4907, 5973, 6920, 7920, 8920, 9920, 10960 and 11960ms. Each event here is one CHORD, not one strum: the chord identity does not change across its two strums, and the re-strum is an internal re-articulation. Boundaries were measured from the RMS envelope (first frame after the inter-chord trough where energy begins a sustained climb), not from the chord classifier, whose segmentation is the thing under test. Durations run 960-1093ms. The final D decays to genuine silence at 12493ms, ~580ms before the file ends at 13076ms, so its end is a real detectable decay rather than a file cutoff. Timestamps are quantized to the engine's analysis hop (640 samples @48kHz = 13.3ms) so every boundary lands on a frame the engine can actually emit.
